category_title: Highly gifted African-American male masking ability for social acceptance
minimal_context: Jimmy is in his English class with his peers and is expected to complete and submit a writing assignment.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Jimmy, we are starting the English writing assignment now. Please get your paper out and begin working.

STUDENT: (Keeps his head down on the desk without taking out any materials)

TUTOR: You need to complete the assignment and turn it in so you can get a grade.

STUDENT: I do the work, I just don't turn it in and sometimes I do it in a different way.

TUTOR: If you have the work done, you should just hand it in right now.

STUDENT: (Scoffs) (Puts his head back down to sleep to drown out the classroom environment, refusing to speak or engage any further while his peers are present)

options.A: Require three revisions per English writing assignment in the personal composition notebook, and only grade the final, third draft when the student submits their coursework.
options.B: View gifted underachievers as potential achievers struggling for a specific reason, not just by choice. Remove the tendency to blame the student, and view underachievement in English class as a promise for potential.
options.C: Require the student to use their personal composition notebook to take notes, organize their writing assignments, and archive past English coursework during the class periods.
options.D: Implement relatively tight timelines for completing and submitting all English writing assignments and coursework, requiring the student to finish their work during the class periods.
